heading: What Tachyon trusts and checks
body:
A `CatalogService.js` runs everywhere and uses browser APIs. A `CatalogService.swift` runs on Apple targets. It uses the platform SDK with the operating system permissions of the host process. Native service code is trusted application code. Tachyon does not sandbox it (run it in a restricted area). The bridge between the page and the service is a separate boundary. Before the host runs a supported member operation, it checks three things. They are the local origin, the main frame and the canonical route (the one official form of the route). The page names the operation by the instance name of the service. Manifest grants still control which window API the page can use, and which browser APIs that need consent (clipboard, share, notifications, geolocation) the page gives to services (`tac.browserApis`).

At build time, Tachyon also checks that a service which runs as WebAssembly does not call the browser itself. A Swift service that imports JavaScriptKit fails with TY1317. The error names the file and the word to remove.
